item.title: Link to "Top Rated Pages" in sidebar?: Re: Link to "Top Rated Pages" in sidebar?
item.content:encoded:
For new readers, a link to the top rated pages of all time seems like a great place to start.

Is there a particular reason why there isn't a link to it in the sidebar?

I believe the initial decision was made because there was a fairly noticeable bloat in votes and attention going to the articles that had already been popular for years.

Many of the highest rated pages on the site are articles written almost a decade ago, which aren't up to the standards expected of current works.

If a new reader is insistent on focusing on the highest rated pages on the entirety of the site, they need only scroll down to the archive section of the "Top Rated New Pages" page.

item.title: Link to "Top Rated Pages" in sidebar?: Link to "Top Rated Pages" in sidebar?
item.content:encoded:
The sidebar, under "Discover Content", has a link to "Top Rated New Pages", but there is no link to "Top Rated Pages": http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/top-rated-pages

For new readers, a link to the top rated pages of all time seems like a great place to start.

Is there a particular reason why there isn't a link to it in the sidebar?

If not, could an admin please add one, under Discover Content?

Thanks!

item.title: Why has the Heritage Collection died?: Re: Why has the Heritage Collection died?
item.content:encoded: It was very controversial with not a lot of people liking the idea. The reasons people didn't like it are numerous, and some searching through the threads will reveal those reasons. Because of that, the Collection was not added to and has since been archived for historical purposes.

item.title: Why has the Heritage Collection died?: Re: Why has the Heritage Collection died?
item.content:encoded:
The Heritage Collection was controversial from birth: it was, in practice, more of a popularity thing than anything. If you want to see displays of good SCPs decided by the community, go to User Curated Lists. If you want to see something fresh, check out Underread and Underrated.

Recently, Rewrite Team, which has jurisdiction over this, has decided to remove the rating module from articles and left the page up for posterity: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-752031/heritage-collection-arc#post-4799999

item.title: Why has the Heritage Collection died?: Re: Why has the Heritage Collection died?

item.title: New fairer voting system: Re: New fairer voting system
item.content:encoded:
Talked this over with other staff for a bit and we're not interested in implementing this idea, since it would be rather disruptive to the reading experience and not really possible given Wikidot's infrastructure. Voting as it exists now is a very passive and reader-driven experience, almost an afterthought, so most people probably aren't going to be on board for making it a more active and structured system.

Moreover, while Wikidot can handle randomness somewhat, it's rather finicky and there's not really a way to weight probability based on vote count. There just isn't a reasonable way to implement what you're describing.

… while dramatically good new articles can't ever hope to catch up over time due to the very existence of the "http://www.scpwiki.com/top-rated-pages" page unless the reader really wants to read more than 1000 articles.

Top Rated Pages isn't generally how people discover popular articles; most of those are rated so high because they have some presence outside of the community on Reddit, YouTube, etc., or they were written by a popular author, or any other number of reasons. While the goal of promoting newer works is admirable, this solution wouldn't be particularly effective in curtailing that behavior.

item.title: New fairer voting system: New fairer voting system
item.content:encoded:
I feel a NEW voting system based on upvotes-per-view would stop good and nostalgic but not awesome ancient articles from being so very dramatically advantaged on top lists, while dramatically good new articles can't ever hope to catch up over time due to the very existence of the "http://www.scpwiki.com/top-rated-pages" page unless the reader really wants to read more than 1000 articles.

We need a system like this one.
http://www.kittenwar.com/
You can tell the "losingest" kittens are not there just because they are new, and the "winningest" kittens aren't there because they are old, this system does a better job of ranking quality than the current system.

The system would require:
-Knowing which SCP numbers are not a 404 or empty page or administrative issues page.

-The reader is shown 2 article links, they open in a new tabs. The first is fully random (to be fair), and the other is bias toward articles that showed up less in the NEW voting system 20 percent of the time, and fully random the rest of the time.

-The reader is asked after reading both articles to return to the tab of origin and pick which one they prefer.

-The best articles will win more "SCPfights".

-If you don't do it, some extrernal site will and will have ads on top of the "rate my SCP!" voting thingy.

Thoughts?

item.title: Rules and You, a Bright (TM) Poll: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
I don't really see any harm in posting the Sandbox, especially if the author feels more comfortable with it than summarizing as a proposal.

Reviewers in the concept critique forum are present to critique concepts, not drafts. The point of having the "only provide a sandbox link if asked" rule is to ensure that authors don't inadvertently make it more difficult for reviewers to assist them.

If a reviewer has a question about the basic premise of a piece, it's much more conducive to the review process if the author can quickly and directly answer said question, rather than the author just having the reviewer dig through the entirety of a draft to maybe (not always, in the case of drafts with many errors or written unclearly) find clues.

I tend to write my SCP idea as a Sandbox before making a proposal for it, so I feel like that my "summary" of my SCP idea may not be as good as the Sandbox.

If you are looking for sandbox critique without going through the greenlighing process, you can use the IRC chatrooms. Please note that you may still be asked to quickly summarize your core concept, especially if there are multiple authors seeking feedback at the same time and reviewers need to decide which they can reasonably commit to providing assistance for.

item.title: Rules and You, a Bright (TM) Poll: Re: Rules and You, a Bright (TM) Poll
item.content:encoded: One rule that I don't like is not being allowed to post Sandboxes in SCP proposals without being asked. I tend to write my SCP idea as a Sandbox before making a proposal for it, so I feel like that my "summary" of my SCP idea may not be as good as the Sandbox. Plus, I don't really see any harm in posting the Sandbox, especially if the author feels more comfortable with it than summarizing as a proposal.
